title: Rent to Own Gaming PC: What It Really Costs and Better Options
description: A rent-to-own gaming PC often costs 2 to 3 times its cash price by the last payment. How lease-to-own works, the real cost, and 6 cheaper ways to pay.
dek: How lease-to-own and gaming PC rental work, what you pay by the end, and the financing, used and cloud options that cost less.
quickAnswer: Rent-to-own lets you take a gaming PC home with no credit check and small weekly or monthly payments, but by the final payment you often pay two to three times the cash price. A 0% intro APR card, store financing or buy now pay later costs far less if you qualify. With no credit, a used PC or a cheaper prebuilt is usually the better deal, and cloud gaming is the cheapest true rental.
intro: This page explains how rent-to-own and lease-to-own gaming PCs work, works through what one costs by the last payment, and compares it with every other way to pay for a gaming PC over time, from store financing to cloud gaming.

The payment examples are hypothetical and labeled as such, because lease terms vary by store, state and the price of the PC. Always read the total cost of ownership on the agreement, which lease-to-own sellers are generally required to disclose, before you sign.

sections.h: How Does Rent to Own a Gaming PC Work?
body: Rent to own is a lease with an option to buy. You sign a lease-purchase agreement, pay an initial amount and then make weekly, biweekly or monthly payments. You can usually return the PC and stop paying at any time, and you own it once every payment is made, or earlier if you use the early purchase option the agreement lists.

Because it is a lease rather than a loan, it usually does not require a credit check, which is the main reason people use it. The trade-off is price. The lease payments are set so the seller profits even when customers return the item early, so the total you pay to own it is far higher than the cash price.

You will see two kinds of sellers: rent-to-own stores with physical locations, and online lease-to-own providers that appear as a payment option at checkout on electronics retailers' sites. Both work the same way, and both must show the total cost to own on the agreement. That figure, not the weekly payment, is the number to compare.

sections.h: How Much Does a Rent-to-Own Gaming PC Really Cost?
body: By the last payment, a rent-to-own gaming PC often costs two to three times its cash price. The table below shows how a hypothetical $1,000 gaming PC compares across payment methods. The lease-to-own and financing figures are illustrative examples, not quotes from any provider; your agreement will show the real numbers.

The gap comes from the payment schedule. In the example, a $55 weekly payment looks small, but over 52 weeks it adds up to $2,860. Even the early purchase option, which many agreements offer at a discount within the first few months, usually costs noticeably more than the cash price.

The 30 percent APR loan is an example of a high-rate store card or personal loan; it costs far more than paying cash, but still far less than the lease in this example. A 0% intro APR offer paid off in time costs nothing extra at all.

sections.h: Is Renting a Gaming PC Worth It?
body: Renting to own a gaming PC is rarely worth it if you have any other option. It makes sense in a narrow case: you have no credit or poor credit, you cannot wait to save up, and you are confident you will use the early purchase option within a few months, which is where the markup is smallest.

It also makes some sense if you genuinely only want a gaming PC for a short time, such as a few weeks over a holiday, and plan to return it. Then you are paying a rental fee for use, not for ownership, and the total-cost figure matters less.

For everyone else, the money is better spent on a cheaper machine bought outright. A $2,860 total cost would build a strong 1440p gaming PC with an [RX 9070 XT](/gear/rx-9070-xt/) and still leave change, according to our [gaming PC cost breakdown](/how-much-does-a-gaming-pc-cost/).

sections.h: Does Rent to Own Affect Your Credit?
body: Usually not in your favor. Many lease-to-own providers do not report on-time payments to the major credit bureaus, so paying on time often does not build your credit score. Missed payments, however, can be sent to collections, and a collections account does show up and hurts your score.

Some providers do report, and some run a soft credit check at signup that does not affect your score; the agreement or the provider's FAQ will say which. If building credit is part of your goal, a secured credit card or a credit-builder loan does that more directly than a lease.

sections.h: What Are the Best Alternatives to Rent-to-Own Gaming PCs?
body: The best alternative depends on your credit and how much you can put down. In rough order of total cost, from cheapest to most expensive:

Save for two or three months and buy outright. A capable 1080p gaming PC costs about $750 to $1,000 to build, and a discounted prebuilt can be close to that; see [best budget gaming PC](/best-budget-gaming-pc/) and [best gaming PC under $1,000](/best-gaming-pc-under-1000/).

Use a 0% intro APR credit card or a retailer's promotional financing, and pay it off before the promo ends. Watch for deferred interest: some store financing charges all the interest back to the purchase date if any balance remains when the promotion ends.

Use buy now, pay later for a cheaper PC. Pay-in-4 plans typically charge no interest when paid on time; longer plans may charge interest. Treat each plan as debt even though it feels like a payment schedule.

Buy used. A used PC with an RTX 2060, RTX 3060 or RX 6600-class card often sells for less than half of a new one with similar performance. Our [old GeForce equivalents](/old-nvidia-gpu-equivalents/) and [AMD vs NVIDIA equivalents](/amd-vs-nvidia-gpu-equivalents/) charts show what those cards match today.
Start smaller and upgrade. A PC with an [RX 6600](/gear/rx-6600/) or [Arc B580](/gear/arc-b580/) now, and a better graphics card next year, spreads the cost without any interest.

sections.h: Can You Rent a Gaming PC Through the Cloud Instead?
body: Yes, and it is the cheapest way to rent gaming PC performance. Cloud gaming services run your games on a remote gaming PC and stream the video to a laptop, TV, phone or old desktop. NVIDIA's GeForce NOW offers a free tier with session limits and paid tiers that have cost roughly $10 to $20 a month; check NVIDIA's site for current tiers and prices.

Cloud gaming works with games you already own on supported stores, so you still buy your games. You need a fast, stable internet connection, and fast competitive shooters feel the added delay more than slower games. If that fits, a year of a top cloud tier costs a fraction of a lease-to-own PC, with nothing to return.

sections.h: How Do You Finance a Gaming PC With Bad Credit?
body: With bad or no credit, the cheapest route is usually a smaller purchase you can pay for outright, or a used PC. If you need to spread payments, compare a lease-to-own agreement's total cost against a pay-in-4 plan on a cheaper PC, which some buy now, pay later services approve without a hard credit check.

A credit union's small personal loan is another option worth asking about, since credit unions often lend at lower rates than store cards. Whatever you choose, compare the total paid, not the payment, and make sure the PC is worth that total: our [gaming PC cost guide](/how-much-does-a-gaming-pc-cost/) shows what each performance tier costs in parts.

sections.h: What Should You Check Before Signing a Lease-to-Own Agreement?
body: Check five things on the agreement before you sign: the total cost to own, the number and size of payments, the early purchase option and its deadline, what happens if you miss a payment, and who pays for repairs during the lease.

Then check the PC itself. Lease-to-own listings sometimes use older or lower-tier parts at a high cash price, which makes the total cost even worse. Compare the listed CPU and graphics card with our [prebuilt gaming PC guide](/best-prebuilt-gaming-pc/) and the [console GPU equivalents](/console-gpu-equivalents/) chart, and confirm the power supply, memory and storage are named. A gaming PC that cannot run your games well is expensive at any price.

mistakes: Comparing weekly payments instead of total cost
A $55 weekly payment sounds smaller than a $1,000 price tag, but over a year it can total almost three times as much. Always compare the total cost to own printed on the agreement.
Many agreements offer a much lower buyout price in the first few months. Miss that deadline and you are on the full schedule. Put the date in your calendar the day you sign.
A lease multiplies the cash price, so a PC that was overpriced to begin with becomes very expensive. Check the parts against a fair price before you look at payment terms.
Many lease-to-own providers do not report on-time payments to the credit bureaus, but missed payments can go to collections. Do not count on a lease to raise your score.
Ignoring deferred interest on store financing
Some promotional financing charges all the interest back to day one if a balance remains when the promo ends. Pay it off early, or choose a true 0% APR card instead.
bottomLine: Rent to own gets a gaming PC into your home with no credit check, but the total often reaches two to three times the cash price, and on-time payments may not build your credit. If you qualify, 0% financing or buy now, pay later costs nothing extra; if you do not, a used PC, a cheaper prebuilt or cloud gaming is usually the better deal. If you do sign a lease, use the early purchase option and compare the total cost to own, not the weekly payment.

faqs.q: Can you rent to own a gaming PC?
faqs.a: Yes. Rent-to-own stores and online lease-to-own providers offer gaming PCs on lease-purchase agreements with weekly or monthly payments, usually without a credit check. You own the PC after the final payment or by using the early purchase option.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to rent a gaming PC?
faqs.a: It varies by provider and PC, but lease-to-own payments for a mid-range gaming PC can run in the range of $150 to $250 a month (an illustrative example; terms vary widely), and the total cost to own often reaches two to three times the cash price. Cloud gaming costs from free to about $20 a month.

faqs.q: Is rent to own a gaming PC a good idea?
faqs.a: Usually not, because the total cost is much higher than buying outright or using 0% financing. It can make sense only if you have no credit, cannot save up first, and use the early purchase option within the first few months.

faqs.q: Does rent to own build credit?
faqs.a: Often not. Many lease-to-own providers do not report on-time payments to the major credit bureaus, though missed payments can be sent to collections and hurt your score. Check the provider's policy before signing.

faqs.q: Can I finance a gaming PC with no credit check?
faqs.a: Yes, through lease-to-own agreements and some buy now, pay later plans that use a soft check or none at all. Lease-to-own costs far more in total; a pay-in-4 plan on a cheaper PC is usually the better no-credit option.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way to get a gaming PC with monthly payments?
faqs.a: A 0% intro APR credit card or promotional store financing paid off in time costs nothing extra. Buy now, pay later pay-in-4 plans are also interest-free when paid on schedule. Both are far cheaper than lease-to-own.

faqs.q: Is cloud gaming cheaper than renting a gaming PC?
faqs.a: Yes, much cheaper. Services such as GeForce NOW run games on remote gaming PCs for free or roughly $10 to $20 a month, though you need fast internet and must own your games. Check current pricing on the provider's site.

faqs.q: Can you rent a gaming PC for a week or a month?
faqs.a: Some rental providers and rent-to-own stores allow short rentals that you return, though availability varies by area. For short-term play, cloud gaming is usually simpler and cheaper, with nothing to return.
